mainTopic: Omens and good signs; the קטורת: liability for blending it, מעילה after a מצוה is done, its recipe, and the rule that it is prepared only in the מקדש
overview: The amud opens by finishing a side discussion about omens. A traveler's reflection test is rejected because a bad result could make him lose heart. אביי then teaches the ראש השנה סימנים, and רב משרשיא gives his sons advice about learning and living. The amud then shows that kings anointed from a horn had lasting kingdoms. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה's case of one who blends the קטורת: blending it to smell brings כרת, and smelling it is מעילה. That leads to a discussion of whether there is מעילה once an item's מצוה is done, and of the rule that two פסוקים teaching the same thing do not set a general rule, both according to the רבנן and according to רבי דוסא. A ברייתא then gives the full recipe of the קטורת, which supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that all its preparation must be done in the מקדש. A challenge from a משנה about consecrated property is answered first by רבי אושעיא and then, after רב יוסף rejects that answer, by רב יוסף himself. The amud ends by explaining how much קטורת was made each year and how the leftover was given to the craftsmen as wages.

steps.title: The reflection omen for a traveler
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes an omen: if a traveler sees a reflection of a reflection of his reflection, he will return home.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sees a reflection of a reflection of his reflection, he will know that he will come back home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an omen that began just before this point. A person going on a trip can test whether he will return home by looking for a layered reflection of himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sentence is the second half of a longer statement. It gives the sign itself: seeing a reflection of a reflection. That sign is supposed to mean that the traveler will come home safely.

keyTerms.meaning: A reflection or shadow-image of a person
He will know
That he will come back to his home

phrases.english: a reflection of a reflection of a reflection,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started just before this point, about a traveler who wants to know if he'll get home.

phrases.english: he will know that he will come to his home.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּבוּאָה לְבָבוּאָה דְבָבוּאָה, נִידַּע דְּאָתֵי לְבֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the omen statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a layered reflection is a sign that the traveler will return home.

steps.title: Rejecting the reflection test
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this test should not be done, because a bad result could make the person lose heart and bring him bad luck.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is nothing, because maybe he will become discouraged, and his fortune will turn bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the omen from Step 1. It says a person should not do this test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not whether the sign works. The problem is what happens if the person does not see the good sign: he may become discouraged. That discouragement itself can harm him and turn his luck bad.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is nothing; it should not be relied on or practiced
His mind becomes weak; he loses heart
Fortune or luck
Becomes broken or turns bad

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying signs have no meaning at all. The worry is the person's own fear, which could hurt him. In fact, the very next step builds on the idea that a סימן does matter.

phrases.english: But this is nothing,
perhaps he will become discouraged,
and his fortune will turn bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא, דִּילְמָא חָלְשָׁא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects putting the omen from Step 1 into practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects actually doing the reflection test, not the idea that signs mean something.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bad result could discourage the person, and that discouragement itself could bring him bad fortune.

steps.title: אביי: eat foods of good omen on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that since a סימן matters, a person should get used to eating certain fast-growing foods at the start of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Now that you have said a sign is something real, a person should be in the habit of eating, at the start of the year, gourd, fenugreek, leeks, beets, and dates.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the idea that signs matter and turns it into a practical custom. On ראש השנה, a person should eat certain foods as good signs for the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a risky test like the reflection, אביי suggests a positive sign that cannot discourage anyone. These foods grow and multiply quickly, so eating them is a good sign for the coming year. This is the source of the סימנים many people eat on ראש השנה night.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or omen
The start of the year, ראש השנה
Gourd
Fenugreek (some say black-eyed peas)
Leeks, beets, and dates

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש השנה סימנים come from אביי's statement here: since a סימן matters, eat foods that hint at a good, growing year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the basis for the widespread custom of eating סימנים on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now that you have said that a sign is something real,

phrases.aramaic: יְהֵא רְגִיל אִינִישׁ לְמֵיכַל רֵישׁ שַׁתָּא
phrases.english: a person should be accustomed to eat at the start of the year
gourd and fenugreek,
leeks, beets, and dates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ סִימָנָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that signs matter and applies it in a positive, safe way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should get used to eating gourd, fenugreek, leeks, beets, and dates on ראש השנה as good signs.

steps.title: רב משרשיא's advice to his sons on how to learn
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא tells his sons to prepare the משניות before class, to watch their teacher's mouth, and to learn near flowing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to his sons: When you want to go learn before your teacher, first review the משניות, and then go up to your teacher. When you sit before your teacher, look at your teacher's mouth, as it says: 'And your eyes shall see your teacher.' And when you learn a teaching, learn it by water, so that just as the water keeps flowing, your learning will keep flowing.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing with good signs and good habits, רב משרשיא gives his sons three tips for learning well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two tips are practical: come prepared, and watch the teacher closely, which he supports with a פסוק. The third tip is a סימן: learning by flowing water is a good sign that your learning will continue and keep going.

keyTerms.meaning: Review or study (by going over the text)
First, beforehand
The משניות, the basic text
His mouth
A teaching or הלכה being learned
Flow, continue

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said to his sons:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי בָּעֵיתוּ לְמֵיזֵל לְמִגְמַר קַמֵּי רַבְּכוֹן,
phrases.english: When you want to go to learn before your teacher,
first review the mishnayot
and then go up before your teacher.
And when you sit before your teacher,
look at your teacher's mouth,
as it is stated: "And your eyes shall see your teacher."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:20

phrases.english: And when you learn a teaching,
learn it by the water,
so that just as the water flows on,
your learning will flow on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of good signs, now applied to Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prepare the משניות first, watch your teacher's mouth, and learn by flowing water as a good sign that your learning will continue.

steps.title: Better a humble place with Torah than a fancy one; better plain food than harsh spice
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא adds that living on the garbage heaps of מתא מחסיא is better than the palaces of פומבדיתא, and spoiled fish is better than a very harsh spicy dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Better to sit on the garbage heaps of מתא מחסיא and not in the palaces of פומבדיתא. Better to eat spoiled fish than כותח that knocks rocks loose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא gives his sons more advice about where to live and what to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sayings compare something plain or even unpleasant with something that looks better but is worse for you. A humble place in מתא מחסיא is better than a palace in פומבדיתא. Spoiled fish is better than כותח, a dip so sharp it is described as knocking rocks loose.

keyTerms.meaning: Garbage heaps
Palaces
Spoiled, rotten fish
כותח, a sharp, strong-tasting dip
That throws rocks, a picture of how harsh it is

steps.whatToRemember: This section moves from omens (the reflection test, which is rejected) to positive signs (ראש השנה foods, learning by water) and ends with practical life advice from רב משרשיא.

phrases.english: On the garbage heaps of Mata Meḥasya,
phrases.notes: The words "better to sit" are left out but understood: better to live on the garbage heaps here.

phrases.english: and not in the palaces of Pumbedita.
Better spoiled fish
to eat than kutḥa that throws rocks.
phrases.notes: He means it's so sharp and strong it seems to knock rocks loose.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקִּילְקֵי דְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא, וְלָא אַפַּדְנֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב משרשיא's advice to his sons with two more sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble place in מתא מחסיא is better than a palace in פומבדיתא, and spoiled fish is better than harsh כותח.

steps.title: Horn versus jug: anointing as a sign of a lasting kingdom
steps.stepSummary: From חנה's words 'my horn is raised up,' the גמרא shows that kings anointed from a horn had lasting kingdoms, and kings anointed from a jug did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה prayed: 'My heart rejoices in ה׳, my horn is raised up.' She said 'my horn,' not 'my jug.' דוד and שלמה were anointed from a horn, and their kingship lasted. שאול and יהוא were anointed from a jug, and their kingship did not last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more example of a good sign. Being anointed from a horn was a sign that the kingship would last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא notices the exact word חנה chose: 'horn' (קרן), not 'jug' (פך). History bears it out. The horn-anointed kings started dynasties that lasted, and the jug-anointed kings did not. This fits the earlier steps, which said that סימנים (signs) matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn; the container used to anoint דוד and שלמה
Jug or flask; the container used to anoint שאול and יהוא
They were anointed
Their kingship continued (it lasted)

steps.whatToRemember: Horn means a lasting kingdom (דוד, שלמה). Jug means a kingdom that did not last (שאול, יהוא). This closes the discussion of signs.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the wordplay. נִמְשְׁחוּ means 'anointed' and נִמְשְׁכָה means 'continued.' The two words look alike, but they are different.

phrases.english: "And Hannah prayed and said:
My heart exults in the Lord, my horn is exalted"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:1

phrases.english: "My horn is exalted," and not "my jug is exalted"
David and Solomon, who were anointed with a horn
their kingship lasted
Saul and Jehu, who were anointed from the jug
their kingship did not last.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמָה קַרְנִי וְלֹא רָמָה פַּכִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about good signs, now tied to the anointing oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being anointed from a horn is a sign of a lasting kingship. Being anointed from a jug is not.

steps.title: Blending the incense: when one is liable and when one is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of one who blends the קטורת. A ברייתא explains that it depends on his purpose, and that someone who only smells it has done מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who blends the incense.' The רבנן taught: if he blends it to learn how, or to give it to the community, he is exempt. If he blends it in order to smell it, he is liable. One who smells the incense is exempt, but he has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a ברייתא. The ברייתא explains when blending the קטורת brings כרת and what happens to someone who only smells it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blending the קטורת is only forbidden when it is done in order to enjoy its smell. Blending to practice, or to hand it over for the בית המקדש, is allowed. Someone who just smells it does not get כרת, but he has used holy property for his own benefit, which is מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who blends or compounds (the spices)
The incense offered in the בית המקדש
To hand it over to the community (for use in the בית המקדש)
To smell (for one's own enjoyment)
He committed מעילה: wrongly benefiting from holy property

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' here only means no כרת and no חטאת. The person who smells is still not innocent, because he has committed מעילה.

phrases.english: "One who blends the incense."
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה, which listed this person among those who get כרת.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who blends the incense to learn with it
or to hand it over to the community is exempt
if to smell it, he is liable.
And one who smells it is exempt
except that he has misused holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְפַטֵּם אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: back to the halachic list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blending in order to smell brings כרת. Blending to learn or for the community is exempt. Smelling brings no כרת but is מעילה.

steps.title: Challenge: smell has no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how smelling can be מעילה, when בר קפרא taught that sound, sight and smell have no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really מעילה here? But רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: sound, sight and smell have no מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last line of the ברייתא. A different teaching says plainly that smell can never be מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא's rule is that hearing, seeing or smelling something holy is not a real use of it, so it is not מעילה. That seems to contradict the ברייתא, which said that one who smells the קטורת has committed מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there really...? (opens a challenge)
Misuse of holy property
Sound, sight and smell

phrases.english: And is there misuse of holy property?
But didn't Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Bar Kappara:
Sound, sight and smell
are not subject to misuse of holy property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא מְעִילָה? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's statement that one who smells has committed מעילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּעַל' about one who smells the קטורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בר קפרא's general rule says smell is never מעילה, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: Answer: only the smell after the smoke rises is free of מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא splits smell into two stages. After the smoke column rises, the מצוה is done, so there is no מעילה. Before that, there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The smell after the column of smoke has risen has no מעילה, because there is nothing that can be the subject of מעילה once its מצוה has been done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that בר קפרא and the ברייתא are speaking about different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא's rule covers the smell after the smoke column rises. By then the מצוה of the קטורת is complete, and nothing is subject to מעילה after its מצוה is done. The ברייתא covers the smell before that, while the קטורת is still in use, and that smell is מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its column of smoke (rising like a palm tree)
Its מצוה has been done
One is liable for misusing it

steps.whatToRemember: Smell of the קטורת before the smoke rises is מעילה. After the smoke rises, it is not, because once a thing's מצוה is done there is no מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step teaches a general rule: an item is no longer subject to מעילה once its מצוה has been done.

phrases.english: Smell after its column of smoke has risen
phrases.notes: This hints that the smell before the smoke rises is still מעילה. That is the case the ברייתא was talking about.

phrases.english: is not subject to misuse of holy property,
for you have no item that, afterward,
once its מצוה has been done, is still subject to misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵיחַ אַחַר שֶׁתַּעֲלֶה תִּמְרָתוֹ אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by limiting בר קפרא's rule to the smell after the smoke rises.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the two sources speak about different times (before and after the smoke rises).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Smell is never מעילה, so the ברייתא seems wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Smell before the smoke rises is מעילה. Smell after it rises is not, because the מצוה is already done.

steps.title: Challenge from the removal of the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that there is no מעילה once a מצוה is done. תרומת הדשן has finished its מצוה, yet there is still מעילה on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say there is מעילה even after the מצוה is done? Look at the removal of the ashes: its מצוה is done, and still there is מעילה on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 9 that once a מצוה is finished there is no מעילה. It brings a case where the מצוה is finished and there is still מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes on the מזבח come from קרבנות that were already burned, so their מצוה is complete. Even so, the תורה treats the ashes as still holy, and using them is מעילה. That seems to break the rule that a finished מצוה ends מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily removal of a portion of ashes from the מזבח
Misusing הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
Its מצוה has already been done
But look at this case, which seems to contradict

phrases.english: And why not?
phrases.notes: He means: why not say there is מעילה even after the מצוה is done?

phrases.english: But there is the removal of the ashes,
whose מצוה has been done,
and yet one is liable for מעילה with it!
phrases.notes: This comes from ויקרא 6:3, where the ashes are placed beside the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא? וַהֲרֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle used in Step 9's answer: no מעילה after a מצוה is done.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that once an item's מצוה is done, there is no more מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: תרומת הדשן has a completed מצוה, yet there is still מעילה on it.

steps.title: Two verses teaching the same thing do not set a rule
steps.stepSummary: תרומת הדשן and the בגדי כהונה of יום הכפורים both teach מעילה after the מצוה is done. Since two פסוקים teach the same thing, they are exceptions and not a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The removal of the ashes and the כהן גדול's garments are two פסוקים that teach the same thing, and any two פסוקים that teach the same thing do not teach a general rule for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. It says תרומת הדשן is a special exception, not proof of a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה wanted every finished מצוה to keep מעילה, it would have said so once, and we would learn all other cases from there. Saying it twice, for the ashes and for the garments, shows these two cases are exceptions. So the general rule stays: once the מצוה is done, there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two פסוקים that teach the same law
They do not teach a general rule for other cases
Priestly garments, here the white linen garments of יום הכפורים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for learning from פסוקים across ש״ס: when the תורה repeats the same law in two places, the law stays limited to those cases.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the priestly garments
phrases.notes: These are the white linen garments the כהן גדול wears on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10's challenge by limiting תרומת הדשן to an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the counter-example to an exception, using the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן proves that a finished מצוה still has מעילה in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן and the בגדי כהונה are two exceptions, so no general rule is learned from them. The rule of no מעילה after the מצוה stands.

steps.title: But what about רבי דוסא's view?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the רבנן, who hold the garments need גניזה. But according to רבי דוסא, the garments do not count as a second פסוק, so the answer falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the רבנן. But according to רבי דוסא, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. It says the answer only works for one side of a מחלוקת. The next step brings the ברייתא that shows this מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer needed two פסוקים: the ashes and the garments. If רבי דוסא holds the garments do not need גניזה, only one פסוק is left, the ashes. One פסוק can be a source for a general rule, so the challenge from תרומת הדשן comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (according to one view)
What is there to say? This answer does not work for him

phrases.english: This works well according to the Rabbis,
but according to Rabbi Dosa,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבָּנַן, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 11's answer by showing it works only for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 11 that the בגדי כהונה are a second פסוק alongside תרומת הדשן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא the garments do not need גניזה, so only the ashes remain. A single פסוק can teach a general rule, and the challenge returns.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute about the garments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the רבנן learn from 'and he shall leave them there' that the garments need גניזה. רבי דוסא says an ordinary כהן may still use them, and the פסוק only means the כהן גדול may not use them on another יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall leave them there' teaches that the garments must be put away (גניזה). רבי דוסא says: they are fit for an ordinary כהן. Then what does 'and he shall leave them there' mean? That the כהן גדול may not use them on another יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the מחלוקת it just mentioned. It shows that רבי דוסא does not hold the garments become forbidden after their מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the garments are a second case of something that stays forbidden after its מצוה is done. For רבי דוסא they stay usable by a regular כהן, so they are not a second case of מעילה. That leaves the ashes as the only פסוק. The next step answers this by pairing the ashes with עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting something away so it is never used
They require
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
What does the פסוק come to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא agrees the כהן גדול cannot reuse the garments on another יום הכפורים. He only disagrees about whether they are forbidden altogether.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And he shall leave them there,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:23

phrases.english: teaches that they require burial.
Rabbi Dosa says:
They are fit for an ordinary priest.
And what does the verse teach by saying "And he shall leave them there"?
That he should not use them
on another יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְהִנִּיחָם שָׁם, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁטְּעוּנִין גְּנִיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that backs up Step 12's claim about רבי דוסא's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי דוסא holds the יום הכפורים garments do not need גניזה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ״וְהִנִּיחָם שָׁם״ (ויקרא 16:23): the רבנן require גניזה, and רבי דוסא allows an ordinary כהן to use them.

steps.title: A new pair for רבי דוסא: תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: For רבי דוסא, the second source is עגלה ערופה, not the בגדי כהונה. Two פסוקים that teach the same thing do not make a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two פסוקים that teach the same thing, and any two פסוקים that teach the same thing do not teach a rule for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 12. For רבי דוסא, it finds a different second source to pair with תרומת הדשן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא does not count the בגדי כהונה as a second source. So the גמרא uses עגלה ערופה, which is also forbidden after its מצוה is done. Two sources still means two exceptions, not a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Two פסוקים that teach the same law. Because the תורה had to say it twice, it shows the law is limited to those cases.
They do not teach, meaning we cannot apply the law to other cases.
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown.
The daily removal of some ashes from the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes and the heifer whose neck is broken are
phrases.notes: This answers the problem for רבי דוסא from Step 12. עגלה ערופה takes the place of the בגדי כהונה.

phrases.english: two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach their law to other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: משום דהוי תרומת הדשן ועגלה ערופה שני כתובין הבאין כאחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 12, using the opinion of רבי דוסא shown in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Swaps in a different second source so the rule of two פסוקים still works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the בגדי כהונה, תרומת הדשן would stand alone and could teach a general rule of מעילה after a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה is the second source, so these remain exceptions.

steps.title: Where we learn that both need burial
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings ברייתות showing that both תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה need גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of תרומת הדשן? A ברייתא says: 'And he shall put it beside the מזבח.' This teaches that it needs burial. What is the case of עגלה ערופה? A ברייתא says: 'And they shall break the calf's neck there in the valley.' This teaches that it needs burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that each of the two cases really is forbidden after its מצוה is done. It shows the פסוק behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק shows the item must be put away and buried, which means no one may use it. This proves both cases are forbidden even after the מצוה. That is why they count as two פסוקים teaching the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting something away and burying it so no one can use it.
They require.
What is it? A question asking for the source.

phrases.english: What is the case of the removal of the ashes?
As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And he shall put it beside the altar,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3

phrases.english: this teaches that they require burial.
What is the case of the heifer whose neck is broken?
As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And they shall break the heifer's neck there in the valley,"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

phrases.english: this teaches that they require burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: תרומת הדשן מאי היא? דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for the two cases named in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are both forbidden even after their מצוה is done
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, based on ויקרא 6:3 and דברים 21:4

steps.title: Even the other opinion agrees, because of two limiting words
steps.stepSummary: Even those who usually learn from two such פסוקים cannot do so here. Each פסוק has a word that limits the law to that one case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says that two פסוקים teaching the same thing do teach other cases, here they certainly do not. That is because there are two limiting words. By תרומת הדשן it says 'and he shall put it,' meaning this, yes, anything else, no. By עגלה ערופה it says 'the one whose neck was broken,' meaning this one, yes, anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible challenge from the opinion that two פסוקים can teach a general rule. It shows that here, each פסוק limits itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that two פסוקים teaching the same thing can still teach other cases. But here each פסוק has a word, 'it' and 'the,' that limits the law to that case alone. So everyone agrees there is no general rule of מעילה after a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in a פסוק that limits a law to a specific case.
Two limiting words.
This one, yes.
Anything else, no.

steps.whatToRemember: There is no general rule of מעילה after a מצוה is done. תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are exceptions, by either opinion about two פסוקים that teach the same thing.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says that two verses that come as one do teach,
here they certainly do not teach,
because there are two limiting words.

phrases.notes: The word "it" is what does the limiting here.

phrases.english: this, yes; anything else, no.
With the heifer whose neck is broken it is written: "The one whose neck was broken"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:6

phrases.english: the broken-necked heifer, yes; anything else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולמאן דאמר שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדין הכא ודאי אין מלמדין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the answer of Step 14 work even for the opposing view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to limiting words in each פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone who learns from two פסוקים teaching the same thing might make מעילה after a מצוה a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק limits itself, so no general rule can be learned.

steps.title: The recipe for the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the spices of the קטורת and how much of each one goes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: the mixing of the קטורת. Balm, onycha, galbanum and frankincense, seventy מנה each. Myrrh, cassia, spikenard and saffron, sixteen מנה each. Costus twelve, bark three, cinnamon nine. Karshina lye, nine קבין. Cyprus wine, three סאין and three קבין. If he has no Cyprus wine, he brings old white wine. Sodom salt, a quarter. A smoke-raising herb, a tiny amount. רבי נתן says: also a tiny amount of Jordan amber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It gives the full recipe for the קטורת burned in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Main spices are measured by weight in units of מנה. The lye and wine are measured by volume in קבין and סאין. רבי נתן adds one more ingredient in a tiny amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixing and preparing of the incense.
A unit of weight.
Units of volume. A סאה equals six קבין.
An herb that makes the smoke rise straight up.
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: The blending of the incense:
The balm, the onycha, the galbanum, and the frankincense:
a weight of seventy, seventy maneh each.
phrases.notes: Literally "seventy of seventy." It means each of these four spices weighs seventy מנה.

phrases.english: Myrrh, cassia, spikenard, and saffron:

phrases.english: a weight of sixteen, sixteen maneh each.
Costus: twelve;

phrases.aramaic: יֵין קַפְרִיסִין – סְאִין תְּלָתָא קַבִּין תְּלָתָא.
phrases.english: Cyprus wine: three se'a and three kav.
If he does not have Cyprus wine,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת is made of fixed spices in fixed amounts, along with lye, wine, salt and a smoke-raising herb.

steps.title: Honey ruins the קטורת, and leaving out a spice is a capital sin
steps.stepSummary: Adding honey disqualifies the קטורת. Leaving out any of its spices makes a person חייב מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put honey into it, he disqualified it. If he left out any one of its spices, he is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with two rules about making the קטורת wrongly. One rule is about adding something, and one is about leaving something out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding honey makes the קטורת פסול. Leaving out even one spice is much more serious: the person who offers it is חייב מיתה. So the recipe must be complete, with nothing forbidden added.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it unfit.
The spices of the קטורת.
Liable to the death penalty.

phrases.english: And if he put honey into it, he disqualified it.
If he left out any one of all its spices,
he is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם נתן בה דבש פסלה

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honey disqualifies the קטורת. Leaving out a spice makes one חייב מיתה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון explains the balm, the lye and the wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the צרי is sap from a tree. The lye and the wine are used to prepare the צפורן. Urine would also work, but it is not brought into the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the balm is only sap from the balsam tree. Karshina lye is rubbed on the onycha to make it look nice. Cyprus wine is used to soak the onycha so it will be strong. Urine is also good for it, but urine is not brought into the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון explains what some of the ingredients are and what they are used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צרי is the sap, not the wood of the tree. The lye and wine are not spices of their own. They are used to prepare the צפורן, to make it look nice and to make it strong. Urine would do the job, but it is not brought into the מקדש out of respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Sap or resin that drips from a tree.
They rub.
They soak.
Urine.

steps.confusionAlert: The lye and the wine are on the list, but they are not spices burned in the קטורת. They are only used to prepare the צפורן.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַצֳּרִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שְׂרָף מֵעֲצֵי הַקְּטָף.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: The balm is nothing but sap from the balsam trees.

so that it will be strong.
And urine is good for it,

phrases.english: but urine is not brought into the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון אומר הצרי אינו אלא שרף מעצי הקטף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains ingredients listed in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צרי is tree sap. The lye and wine are used to prepare the צפורן, and urine is not used because it is not brought into the מקדש.

steps.title: The previous ruling supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: Because the צפורן was prepared only with materials that may be brought into the מקדש, this supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who says all the work of the קטורת must be done in a holy place.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who learned from the פסוק "It is holy, it shall be holy to you" that all the preparation of the קטורת must be done only in the holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last ruling (urine is not brought into the מקדש) backs up the view of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the צפורן could be prepared outside, using urine would not have been a problem. Since urine was avoided because it cannot enter the מקדש, the preparation must have taken place inside. That matches רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that every step of making the קטורת is done in the holy place.

keyTerms.meaning: supports, backs up
all of its making and preparation
in the holy place, the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that the rest of the section will test: the קטורת may only be prepared inside the מקדש.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,

phrases.english: who says: "It is holy,
it shall be holy to you":
all of its preparation should be done
only in the holy place.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a supporting conclusion from the ruling in step 19 that urine is not brought into the מקדש.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that all preparation of the קטורת must be done in the holy place.

steps.title: A challenge from someone who consecrates all his property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone consecrates his property and it includes items fit for communal offerings, those items are given to the craftsmen as wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a משנה: If a person consecrates his property and it includes items fit for communal offerings, they are given to the craftsmen as their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that it will use to challenge רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. This step only quotes the source; the next step shows where the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's own property is at home, not in the מקדש. If among his things there is something fit for communal offerings, the source treats it as a normal case. The question will be which item this could be.

keyTerms.meaning: one who consecrates his property to the מקדש
communal offerings, brought for all of Israel
craftsmen who worked in the מקדש
as their wages

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who consecrates his possessions,
and among them were items fit
for communal offerings:
they are given to the craftsmen as their wages.
phrases.notes: Giving them as pay takes away their holiness. Then they can be bought back for the right use.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the rule of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that all preparation of the קטורת must be in the holy place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the משנה speaks of a private person's property that includes items fit for communal offerings. The next step will show this must mean קטורת.

steps.title: The only item that fits is קטורת
steps.stepSummary: Animals and wines, oils, and flours are already taught separately, so the items must be קטורת. That would mean a private person made קטורת at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these fit items? If they are animals, that was already taught. If they are wines, oils, and flours, that was also already taught. So isn't it talking about קטורת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out which items the משנה means and concludes it must be קטורת. This is the actual challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other kind of offering material is listed elsewhere in that משנה, so only קטורת is left. If a private person had קטורת among his things, he must have made it outside the מקדש. That goes against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who says it may only be made in the holy place.

keyTerms.meaning: what are they?
domestic animals and wild animals
fine flours, used for מנחות
rather, isn't it…? (a way of pushing to a conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the craftsmen's wages. The problem is that a private person had קטורת at home, which means it was made outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: These fit items, what are they?
If domestic and wild animals,
he already taught them!
phrases.notes: These cases appear later in that same משנה.

phrases.english: If wines, oils, and flours,
he already taught them!
Rather, isn't it קטורת?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי דְּבָרִים הָרְאוּיִין, מַאי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 21 by showing the items must be קטורת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that all preparation of the קטורת is done in the holy place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By elimination the items are קטורת. A private person owning קטורת means it was made outside the מקדש, which contradicts the rule.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: it is קטורת that was given to the craftsmen as wages
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains that the משנה means קטורת made in the מקדש and then given to the craftsmen as pay. A ברייתא about leftover קטורת shows how this happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: It is talking about קטורת that was given to the craftsmen as wages. As a ברייתא teaches: What did they do with leftover קטורת? They set aside from it the amount of the craftsmen's wages, moved its holiness onto the craftsmen's money, gave the קטורת to the craftsmen as pay, and then bought it back with money from the new collection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers the challenge. The קטורת in the man's property was made properly in the מקדש, and only later reached a private person as wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover קטורת was made in the holy place, so רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule was kept. It was then handed to the craftsmen as pay and became their own, non-holy property. If a craftsman later consecrated all his things, that קטורת would be among them, without anyone making קטורת outside.

keyTerms.meaning: in that particular one, that specific case
the leftover קטורת
they set aside
they remove its holiness by moving it onto money
the new collection (of שקלים)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא's answer: the קטורת in a private person's property was made in the מקדש and reached him as wages. רב יוסף rejects this answer in the next step and gives his own in Step 25.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
It refers to that which is given to the craftsmen as their wages.
As it was taught: The leftover קטורת,
what would they do with it?
They would set aside from it the craftsmen's wages,
and move its holiness onto the craftsmen's money,
and give it to the craftsmen as their wages,
and then buy it back from the new collection.
phrases.notes: The new collection is the fresh year's שקלים, used to buy the קטורת back from the craftsmen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: בְּאוֹתָהּ הַנִּיתֶּנֶת לְאוּמָּנִים בִּשְׂכָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 21–22 by narrowing which קטורת the משנה means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה speaks of קטורת made in the מקדש that later reached a craftsman as wages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קטורת in a private person's property must have been made by him outside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was leftover קטורת made in the מקדש, given to the craftsmen as pay, and later consecrated with their property. The rule of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא stands.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה should have mentioned buying it back
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects to רבי אושעיא's answer. Wherever leftovers are discussed, the rule says they are bought back with new-year funds. The משנה about consecrated property does not say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: For all leftovers, the teaching says they go back and buy it from the new collection. But here it does not say that!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the answer from step 23, which said the משנה is about קטורת paid to the craftsmen as wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When leftover holy items are handed out, the standard rule adds that the Temple buys them back with money from the new collection. The משנה about someone consecrating his property leaves this out. So רב יוסף argues that it cannot be talking about leftover קטורת that was paid to craftsmen.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
Leftovers of items bought for the מקדש
The new year's collection of shekel money

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to it:
But regarding all the leftovers, it teaches:
they go back and buy it from the new collection,
and here it does not teach this!
phrases.notes: "Here" means the משנה about a person who consecrates all his property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's answer in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's reading that the משנה is about קטורת given to craftsmen as wages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were leftover קטורת, the משנה should mention buying it back from the new collection, as the rule does for all leftovers. Its silence shows it is not that case.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it means one ingredient of the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new answer. The משנה is talking about a single ingredient of the קטורת, not finished, mixed קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף says: the משנה is talking about one of the ingredients of the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: Having pushed aside רבי אושעיא's answer, רב יוסף offers his own way to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary person can own a single spice that is used in the קטורת. Owning it at home does not mean he made קטורת outside the מקדש. So the משנה no longer contradicts רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who says all the work of the קטורת must be done in a holy place.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier answer and giving a new one)
The spices or ingredients of the קטורת

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's answer: the person consecrated a single spice, not mixed קטורת. That is how רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule stays intact.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef says:
It is about one of the ingredients of the incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 24 rejected with a new case definition
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (an ingredient, not finished קטורת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The items fit for communal offerings were finished קטורת, which a private person made at home
steps.terutzMaskana: They were a single spice of the קטורת, which a private person may own, so no קטורת was made outside the מקדש

steps.title: How much קטורת was made each year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 368 מנה of קטורת were made: 365 for the days of the year and 3 extra for the כהן גדול's handfuls on יום הכפורים. Whatever was left was given to the craftsmen as wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The קטורת was made in an amount of 368 מנה. 365 matched the days of the solar year. Three extra מנה were for the handfuls the כהן גדול brought in on יום הכפורים. The rest was given to the craftsmen as their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the background: why there was leftover קטורת at all, and that it went to the craftsmen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One מנה was burned for each day of the year, and three extra מנה were made so the כהן גדול could take his handfuls from them on יום הכפורים. The ברייתא says that whatever remained was given to the craftsmen as wages. That is the practice רבי אושעיא's answer in step 23 relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of weight equal to 100 dinars
The days of the solar year (365)
His two handfuls (what the כהן גדול takes in on יום הכפורים)
Craftsmen who worked in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The three extra מנה are not a leftover set aside for the craftsmen. They are the supply for the כהן גדול's handfuls on יום הכפורים. Only 'the rest', whatever remained, went to the craftsmen.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: The incense was made
in an amount of three hundred sixty-eight maneh,
three hundred sixty-five of them
corresponding to the days of the solar year,
and three extra maneh,
from which the High Priest brings in
his full handfuls on Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:12

phrases.english: and the rest is given to the craftsmen as their wages.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קְטֹרֶת הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background source behind רבי אושעיא's claim that leftover קטורת was paid to craftsmen
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 368 מנה of קטורת were made: 365 for the days of the year, 3 for the כהן גדול's handfuls on יום הכפורים, and the rest went to the craftsmen as wages.

steps.title: The steps for paying craftsmen with leftover קטורת
steps.stepSummary: A source explains the procedure. They set aside enough leftover קטורת to cover the craftsmen's wages and moved its holiness onto the wage money. They gave the קטורת to the craftsmen, then bought it back with funds from the Temple chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: What did they do with the leftover קטורת? They set aside from it the craftsmen's wages, moved its holiness onto the craftsmen's money, and gave it to the craftsmen as their wages. Then they went back and bought it from the Temple chamber's collection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the ברייתא by bringing a teaching that spells out, step by step, how the leftover קטורת was handed to the craftsmen and then returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy קטורת cannot simply be handed out, so its holiness is first moved onto the money owed to the craftsmen. Only then is the now-ordinary קטורת given to them as pay. The מקדש then buys it back with שקלים funds so it can be used again, and this buying-back step is exactly the detail רב יוסף said was missing from the משנה in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover קטורת at the end of the year
They set aside
They remove the holiness by moving it onto money
The shekel funds collected in the Temple chamber

steps.whatToRemember: Leftover קטורת went through four steps: it was set aside, its holiness was moved onto the wage money, it was given to the craftsmen, and it was bought back with chamber funds.
steps.whyThisMatters: The last step, buying it back, explains רב יוסף's objection: a משנה that really dealt with this leftover קטורת would have mentioned that the Temple buys it back.

phrases.english: As it was taught: The leftover incense,
what would they do with it?
They set aside from it the craftsmen's wages,
and they move its holiness onto the craftsmen's money,
and they give it to the craftsmen as their wages,
and they go back and buy it with funds from the chamber's collection.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: מוֹתַר הַקְּטֹרֶת מָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ברייתא in step 26 by detailing how the leftover reached the craftsmen
steps.raayaObject: That leftover קטורת was given to craftsmen as wages through a set procedure
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching on leftover קטורת: set aside, holiness moved onto money, given to craftsmen, bought back with chamber funds
